$comment: Reviewed licence exceptions for BUILD TOOLING only (CI gate 13, ADR-015).
ADR-015 forbids copyleft because 'an Angular library is compiled and
tree-shaken into the consumer's bundle'. That argument is about SHIPPED
code. A bundler or a d.ts rollup plugin runs on a build machine and ships
nothing, so the same licence carries a different risk there.
An entry here is a decision, not a mute button. Rules:
1. The package must NOT appear in `pnpm licenses list --prod`. The
production scope has no exception path — verify-licences.mjs enforces
that separately and will fail regardless of what is written here.
2. The justification must say why the licence cannot reach a consumer.
3. Removing the dependency is always preferable to adding an entry.
Verified 2026-08-28 against the Phase 1 lockfile: `pnpm licenses list
--prod` reported 9 packages, all MIT / Apache-2.0 / 0BSD. Every entry below

exceptions.justification: Build-time CSS transformer reached through @angular/build. MPL-2.0 copyleft is file-scoped and attaches to lightningcss's own source files, which are never emitted into a TEKAD package or a consumer bundle — the tool processes CSS and exits. Not present in the production dependency tree.
Platform-specific native binary for lightningcss above. Same reasoning; a build-machine binary, never shipped.

Used by ng-packagr to roll up .d.ts files at build time. LGPL applies to the plugin's own code, which is not linked into or emitted with TEKAD output — the plugin reads declaration files and writes declaration files. Not present in the production dependency tree. Flagged for re-review if ng-packagr ever inlines plugin code into its output.
